wy_greenland.blurb: Greenland is a bolted wall along the Old Road in Ten Sleep Canyon, holding sixteen sport routes. Grades begin near 5.9, but most lines fall between 5.11 and 5.13, so it suits climbers already comfortable on hard sport rather than beginners. The stone is compact and tan, and the lines tend to be short, sustained and powerful: gently overhanging low down, easing to slab near the chains, with widely spaced pockets that force big moves. Through most of summer the wall holds shade well into the afternoon, and the walk in is brief, which makes it an easy half-day outing.

wy_south_face_base.blurb: South Face Base lies at the foot of Sugar Loaf in Wyoming's Laramie Range, right where the slab face steepens. Its sixteen routes are mostly bolted, with a few trad lines mixed in. Styles split between steep, crimpy face climbing and routes that follow cracks, corners and bulges, and the face has plenty of texture. Grades run from 5.6 up to the low 5.12s, with most routes between 5.8 and 5.10 and a handful harder. The wall faces south and picks up sun. A rough two-track gets you close, so the walk is modest.

wy_warbonnet_peak.blurb: In the Wind River Range, Warbonnet Peak is a steep tower along the Cirque of the Towers' south rim, high over Jackass Pass. This is a remote alpine objective, not a roadside crag. Most of the routes here are alpine climbs, with grades mostly from 5.10 to 5.12 and a lone easier line, plus a couple of boulder problems. Expect lichen, moss and loose rock on some lines, snow in the gullies early in the season, and frequent afternoon thunderstorms, so an early start matters. The terrain is exposed and serious, and the return can be long.

wy_coke_bottle.blurb: Coke Bottle is a steep, south-facing formation in the southeast-central part of Vedauwoo near Laramie, set in a bulge between Fall Wall and Walt's Wall. It catches sun most of the day. Water streaks run down the face, with big horizontal roofs and cracks that go from finger width to body-swallowing. Most of the fifteen routes are trad with a few sport lines, spanning 5.7 to 5.13, with the largest group around 5.11. The climbing is steep and demanding, especially for anyone short on wide-crack experience. Descents are by rappel or a worn path on the northeast side.

wy_rodeo_wall.blurb: Rodeo Wall is a limestone sport crag above the Snake River canyon, south of Hoback Junction and a short drive from Jackson. It has fifteen bolted routes, nearly all between 5.9 and 5.11, with 5.10 the core grade, which makes it a good pick for moderate climbers. The wall is slightly overhanging to near vertical, and the rock alternates between polished and sharp, so crimping is the main theme. It faces east and falls into shade by mid-afternoon in summer, making it a good evening stop. The hike up is short, and the view of the river is a bonus.
